answer: Use 58 parallel slots: 100,000 / (2,500 x 0.7) = 57.1, rounded up to 58. Run each worker at about 70% of capacity at peak (100,000 / 58 = about 1,724 per second, roughly 69%). If one worker drops out, the remaining 57 run at about 70.2%, so they still keep up. Sizing to 41 workers at about 98% would fall behind on any blip, so the 0.7 target is the headroom that lets one drop out without falling behind. Source: pa_pattern_backpressure_scaling.md, Sizing the partition count.
